title: SLI bootstrapping lifecycle and trace proposals
body:
Purpose
This doc captures a pragmatic lifecycle for bootstrapping SLIs for new inference features (new model variants, routing policies, or cache changes) and proposes a compact trace-tagging ladder to make rollouts + investigations faster with low cardinality impact. The goal: get reliable, actionable SLIs in ~= 2 sprints for medium-priority features and provide a minimal trace footprint for rapid triage.

Scope and constraints
- Target services: hosted-api frontends, routing layer, serving workers (inference), kv-cache, and gateway proxies.
- Constraint: keep high-cardinality tags optional; default to sampled traces with essential context.
- Operational goal: oncall can decide rollback/partial-rollout using 3 compact metrics + 2 trace queries.

SLI bootstrapping lifecycle (practical steps)
1) Discovery (week 0):
   - Quick stakeholder interview: owner, SRE oncall, product PM. Gather failure modes, latency expectations, tenant impact.
   - Create lightweight hypothesis: e.g., "95th token latency increases when kv-hit drops below 85%".
   - Jira starter: ENGOBS-312 (example).

2) Contracting (week 0-1):
   - Define 3 primary SLIs (always): availability (error rate), latency (p95 token or request), correctness proxy (synth returned-check or model-responded flag).
   - Define one supporting metric: kv_cache_warmth or kv_hit_rate for features that touch prefix cache.
   - SLI format (string): "service:hosted-api;sli:latency_p95_token;window:5m;query:v=..." (we keep templates in Confluence).

3) Probe / Probe design (week 1):
   - Synthetic probe for critical path (small prompt representing typical path). Probe cadence: 30s for canary, 5m for baseline.
   - Instrument a microprobe that records both end-to-end time and per-hop timings (see trace ladder).

4) Validation & baselining (week 1-3):
   - Run baseline on canary region and compare to existing model variant baseline for 48–72h.
   - Validate correlations: check that kv_hit_rate drop correlates with token p95 increase using sliding-window scatter in query tool.

5) Rollout gating (week 3+):
   - Use 3 golden signals for rollout gate: (1) p95 latency delta < 15% vs baseline, (2) error rate < 0.05% absolute, (3) correctness proxy regression < 0.5%.
   - If gate fails, capture one representative trace and tag as rollout-failure, then rollback.

6) Operate & iterate (post-rollout):
   - Keep the probe for 2 weeks; after stability reduce probe cadence.
   - If stable, convert SLI from experiment to product SLI and add to SLO ownership roster.

Compact SLI definitions (examples)
- availability_error_rate: "sum(errors) / sum(requests) over 5m, counted by http_status>=500 or model_timeout flag"
- latency_p95_token: "95th percentile of token_latency_ms across successful responses, window 5m, by tenant/route"
- kv_hit_rate: "sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_accesses) over 5m, global and per-tenant quickview"
- correctness_probe_fail: "synthetic probe returned mismatch or schema error, rate per 10m"

Trace ladder: minimal hop taxonomy (for low-cardinality, high-signal traces)
- hop.level: 0..5 (int) 
  - 0: client                      (ingress request metadata, route_id, tenant_id)
  - 1: api-gateway                 (auth, initial routing decision)
  - 2: router/load-balancer        (model_variant, batch_hint)
  - 3: worker-init                 (queue_time_ms, batch_size)
  - 4: model-inference             (decode_time_ms, kv_hit boolean, kv_lookup_ms)
  - 5: postprocess/egress         (serialize_ms, response_size_bytes)

Essential trace tags (keep for all traces):
- trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id (auto)
- tenant_id (hashed), route_id, model_variant, hop.level
- kv_hit (true/false), batch_size (small bucketed: 1,2-8,>8), queue_time_ms (buckets), decode_time_ms (buckets)
- probe_id (if synthetic), rollout_tag (canary/primary/fallback)

Optional (sampled) tags: prompt_hash (only sampled traces), user_id (hashed), full_prompt_length_tokens (buckets)

Trace sampling guidance
- Default sample-rate: 2% for user requests, 100% for synthetic probes.
- Head-sample high-latency traces: if token_latency > p95_threshold then force-sample up to 10% additional.
- Always sample traces where kv_hit=false + latency>p95 (priority for cache investigations).

Dashboard sketch notes (operator-first)
- Dashboard: "SLI rollout quickpane" (compact, one-row-per-route): columns = current_p95, p95_delta_24h, error_rate_5m, kv_hit_5m, probe_status, recent_trace_link
- Heatmap: latency ladder heatmap with hop-level stacked bars (queue vs decode vs egress).
- Microdash: per-tenant microdash that shows p50/p95/p99 token latency, kv_hit_rate, and last N trace IDs (linkable to trace UI).
- Alerting: keep 1 fatal alert (error rate > 0.5% sustained 5m) and 1 early-warning (p95 delta > 25% sustained 10m). Early-warning auto-opens an incident and captures one sampled trace.

Investigation playbook (short)
1) Check rollout quickpane for affected routes.
2) If p95 up, open a trace from the last 5m with hop.level breakdown. Check kv_hit tag first.
3) If kv_hit=false often, correlate with recent KV evictions, TTL changes, or model prefix changes (link to KV runbook).
4) If decode_time dominates, check GPU contention metrics and kernel-selection logs on node_id.

Practical tips / gotchas
- Cardinality: do NOT add free-form strings (prompt text, full user ids) to traces by default. Use hashed ids or sampled capture.
- Metric cost: prefer derived aggregates at ingestion time rather than exploding cardinality with per-tenant daily rollups.
- Backfills: if you need to backfill an SLI for historical baseline, run synthetic probes in a mirrored experiment to recreate baseline rather than re-ingesting huge event data.

Next actions / TODOs
- (Maya) draft SLI templates in Confluence and link to Jira ENGOBS-312 (due 2026-02-20).
- (Diego) PR a small trace tag lib change to add hop.level and kv_hit (ENGOBS-323).
- (Priya) implement synthetic probe for new routing policy and run 72h baseline (OBS-529).

Notes & references
- Related: confluence://obs/sli-standards (template bank), existing probe cookbook in shared drive.
- Slack thread: #obs-probes-thread-2026-02 has experiment notes and sample queries.

If anything in here needs to be formalized into the SLO roster, ping me and we'll pull it into the next oncall runbook iteration.
